utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around the courtroom. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case Number IT-98-29-T, the Prosecutor versus Stanislav Galic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Is the Defence ready to continue the cross-examination of Mr. Philipps?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I would just like to mention that my learned friends have not given me the documents that they promised yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What were these documents exactly?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I gave them a list of the ERN numbers, and my colleague said in the break that he would disclose the documents to me during the day.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: My apologies, Mr. President. I had that bundle yesterday and I had thought I had a spare copy and that the Defence had another copy. I do apologise for that. Perhaps I could hand them over now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. At least that is better than nothing. Under these circumstances, knowing that Mr. Ierace was so glad to give them to you, I think perhaps an extra call would have assisted him in preventing that he would have to apologise this morning, Ms. Pilipovic. Yes, Madam Registrar, would you then please escort Mr. Philipps into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Philipps, may I remind you that you are still bound by the solemn declaration you give at the beginning of your testimony.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Philipps, good morning. Yesterday, towards the end of the session, I asked you a question, whether you knew who gave out tasks in the mortar sector and who was part of the battalion group, who was the commander of the section. First of all, I wanted to ask you whether in the course of the analysis of these documents, whether you knew or had any information about the sector commanders.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: By "sector commanders," I take it you mean section commanders?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Philipps, yes, section commander in the mortar platoon, if there was such a battalion, a mortar battalion, in any of the brigades. So within that battalion, there is a section.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can answer the question how it might be generally, but I have no specific information from the documents relating to the orders from a battalion commander to his mortars.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: As part of the battalion, could you tell us who issued orders to the section commander from the battalion?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Generally speaking, a battalion commander would be responsible for the orders to the mortars that formed part of his battalion.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Philipps, while analysing the documents, did you come across a document based on which you could see that the commander of the brigade issues orders to the section commander?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have not seen a specific document where the brigade commander gives orders to battalion assets, that is, directly to the mortars. However, from the structure we can see that, in some cases, mortars were under the command of the brigade commander, but not those mortars which were a part of the battalions.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Philipps. Mr. Philipps, yesterday when we talked about the 4th Mixed Anti-armour or Anti-tank Regiment, you told us and we see how you presented that on the diagram. This is slide number 64. Would you agree with me that in the 4th Mixed Anti-armour Artillery Regiment would have only anti-armour weapons?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Generally speaking, I would expect to find only anti-armour or anti-tank weapons in a mixed anti-tank artillery regiment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Philipps, may I just interrupt you. I think we asked you yesterday to, if possible, whether you could show the slide Ms. Pilipovic is referring to. I think it is slide 64. Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Philipps, could you explain to us the organisational structure of the 4th Mixed Anti-Tank Artillery Regiment?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only information I have about the structure of the 4th Mixed Anti-Tank Artillery Regiment is shown on slide 64. And as you will see, it shows three artillery batteries. This would be unusual, but was the information with which I was provided.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So you would agree with me that on this chart of yours, the composition of the 4th Mixed Anti-Tank Artillery Regiment is not usual, it is not in accordance with the regulations?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I think I stated yesterday, I tried -- well, I did not use the structures of the 4th JNA Corps to come to my conclusions about the structures of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps. So the composition of the 4th Mixed Anti-Tank Artillery Regiment under the JNA, I did not use that structure to superimpose it upon the Sarajevo Romanija Corps. I would expect, or would have expected, to have seen these three artillery batteries within the mixed artillery regiment rather than the mixed anti-tank artillery regiment. This may be a mistake in the statement, but it is not, in a sense, not up to me to decide that the individual who stated he saw these things is incorrect, unless I have information which contradicts it or shows it to be wrong. That is why I have shown them as unconfirmed with dotted lines.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Philipps, I am asking you these questions because it is something that is a part of your expertise. You are a military expert. I would also like to ask you this question regarding the 4th Mixed Anti-tank Artillery Regiment. This is slide 65. Could you tell us --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: It was the 4th Mixed Artillery Regiment.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us whether it was part of the division?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: To understand your reference to a division, the 4th Mixed Artillery Regiment and the 4th Mixed Anti-Tank Artillery Regiment, as I understand it, formed part of the corps artillery group. But I have only seen one reference to a corps artillery group. Generally speaking, these regiments seem to act independently but under the control of the corps headquarters. I am not quite sure about your reference to a division.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Philipps, while you were analysing the documents, come across a document which would indicate that the 4th Mixed Artillery Regiment had a Howitzer division of 150 millimetres, 122 millimetres, and multi-rocket launcher?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have shown on slide number 65 the information that I have located relating to the 4th Mixed Artillery Regiment, and this shows a series of different batteries, some of which were detached at various times to other brigades and some of which remained part of the 4th Mixed Artillery Regiment.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have information that when we are talking about the artillery battalion which was part of the 4th Mixed Artillery Regiment, that there were two corps artillery groups that were formed; one of them was at the Nisici front and the other one was north of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not aware that there were two different corps artillery groups that had been formed, however, I am aware that some of the artillery was detached and supported operations on the Nisici plateau with the 1st Romanija Infantry Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us which documents you used for your chart for the 4th Mixed Artillery Regiment?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I will just have to consult the index.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Philipps, so that we don't lose time, could you please tell us whether for this kind of information, including slide 64, for the anti-tank and the mixed artillery regiment, did you have one document or did you have several documents?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Looking at the diagram, the fact that there are dotted lines around these units means, to my mind, they are unconfirmed as shown on the legend and, therefore, without looking at the index, I would assume that they are from only one document.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me in view of the fact that you only had one document and that this information is unconfirmed, that this chart, when we are talking about these two artillery regiments, the chart does not correspond to the organisational structure of either of the regiments?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unfortunately, I only have the information in the documents that I used. If there is any further information as to the structure of these organisations, then it is not in my possession.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, in relation to that last question, it would be fair for my learned colleague to indicate to the witness the respects in which the organisational structure is, according to the Defence, incorrect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before doing so, Ms. Pilipovic - I hope you are listening as well, Mr. Philipps - I do understand that if you use a dotted line, you say the information on which I have drawn these conclusions are rather weak and, therefore, the conclusions are just as weak because I didn't find any confirmation, which would mean that the parts with the dotted lines are either true or not true. You are not certain about that and you make some reservation. So, therefore, Ms. Pilipovic, if you ask whether the structure on the slide is not correct, I think the expert witness answered that question already, that he says that, "The only information I have would drive me in this direction to assume that this is true." And, therefore, if you say it is not true, the only possible answer, I think, could be that if there is other information which indicates it is not true, that perhaps Mr. Philipps would easily accept or at least take that information into consideration while again looking at the conclusions, but then it would be conclusions drawn up on other documentary basis. So, therefore, I think it is not very useful to put this question to the witness. But if there is any specific information which you think would contradict this or if you know that it is not true, than please confront the witness with that instead of asking him questions which, according to the testimony until now, could result in only one predictable answer. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. But what I wanted to get from the witness, Mr. Philipps, as a military expert, I expected an answer in which Mr. Philipps would explain what comprises the 4th Mixed Artillery Regiment in accordance with the Rules of the Yugoslav Rules or the Sarajevo Romanija Corps which applied the JNA rules.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is fine. Then please ask him to do so. So the question now is what, according to JNA rules, should be or should have been the composition of certain mixed artillery regiment.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that I already asked that question, but I hope that Mr. Philipps will reply to this question now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can reply to the question by saying that I would expect a regiment, but again whether this applies specifically to the JNA is outside my knowledge, as I did not use the structure of the JNA 4th Corps to put together the structure of the 4th Mixed Artillery Regiment. The information I used were orders signed by General Galic relating to the mixed artillery regiment and instructions regarding the handover of artillery units to other brigades. This is the source of the structure that I have.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Philipps, slide 66, we have got the 4th Light Artillery Regiment for anti-aircraft defence. Was information -- we are talking about slide 66. Was information also not available which could confirm the accuracy of this chart, in view of the fact that you used a dotted line here? This is slide 66.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, the only information that I was able to use on the 4th Light Anti-aircraft Artillery Regiment, in this case, was a Defence document. I have the reference here in front of me. The document is dated the 4th of October, 1993, and is a stamped order issued by the Sarajevo Romanija Corps command on that date, attaching the 1st Light Anti-aircraft Artillery Regiment's 20-millimetre guns to another brigade. And hence I have shown on the chart that on the 4th of October, these weapons were detached to the 1st Romanija Infantry Brigade, using the abbreviation in the original document the "1st RPBR." I have used the original abbreviation in case my interpretation of that abbreviation was incorrect. And that was the only source of weapons for the 4th Light Anti-aircraft Artillery Regiment.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Philipps, slide number 69, the 4th Engineers Battalion. Do you know, did you have information that this battalion was organised according to companies and platoons and not in accordance with groups?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would imagine an engineer battalion would normally be organised into companies and then split from companies into platoons. The source of the structure on page 69 is an order by the then Colonel Stanislav Galic relating to future activities and combat activities of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps. I would have to look up the date of that instruction. The translation of obstacle construction group comes from the B/C/S abbreviations, military abbreviations, I believe, of GZ, EGZ, and GOP. This slide only show as very small part of the engineer battalion.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Philipps, yesterday when we talked about the document about the appointment of Mr. Marko Zubic, who according -- which according to you is a document which you cited in your charts and stated that Mr. Sipcic, according to you, based on that document, was on duty as corps commander during the months of July and August. Do you have this document in front of you?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have a copy of that document in front of me. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the Defence has a copy so I would like to have this document shown to Mr Philipps, and we can also place it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Are you going to tender the document or is it just for the expert witness to...

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we would just like to have Mr. Philipps explain this document to us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please put it on the ELMO, Madam Usher.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Philipps, in the lower right corner of this document, it says, "Commander Major General Tomislav Sipcic"?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that there is no signature of Mr. Sipcic on this document?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there is no signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: A document which bears no signature by the person whose name and surname are on the document, for you as an analyst, what would be the weight of that document if it had no signature?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It has less weight with no signature, but it does have an official stamp and the signature of someone else in the organisation.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: If I put it to you that this document could have been issued as a blanket document, would you then consider it had the same weight if another person had signed it? Basically, does this document prove to you that Mr. Tomislav Sipcic was occupying this post at the time?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. As a single document, it is merely information that Tomislav Sipcic may have been the corps commander at that period of time and would require confirmation from other documents or other sources to put General Tomislav Sipcic as the corps commander at that period.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So, what you are saying is that this information that you have inputted into your charts, that this is the period when Mr. Tomislav Sipcic was a major general and he was the corps commander, this is information which is still unconfirmed?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The positioning of General Sipcic as a corps commander was based on this document and a separate witness statement by the Sarajevo Romanija Corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if I may just confer with my colleagues, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence has nothing further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Pilipovic. Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, just while that document is on the ELMO, might the camera pan up so that we can see the ERN number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. Philipps, you said that you attributed weight to the document in part because of the stamp and the signature. What does the stamp say, for the record?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we have no interpretation. I don't have interpretation and Mr. Galic has no interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So we have first, we will have to solve the technical problem. I see that there is some --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone in the B/C/S booth has still not been fixed, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So we are still facing the problem of only one microphone. We can now continue, but may I ask the technical booth, it is now the second day that there is only one microphone properly functioning in the B/C/S booth, that proper attention will be paid to it during the first break. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. Philipps, I was asking you what words, if any, can be discerned in the stamp, but perhaps going on the ELMO, do these letters appear in the form of a word, "K-o-m-a-n-d" and then is there an "a" after the "d"?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see the words commander, Komanda Korpusa.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Have you seen that stamp before?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have seen that stamp before.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: On what type of documents have you seen that type of stamp before?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is -- I have seen it on documents that relate to documents coming from the corps command of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I ask the witness be shown a two-page document. I have one additional copy. Perhaps that could go to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. Philipps, do you read B/C/S?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can understand one or two military terms, but I have no real understanding of the language.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I hope that the witness does understand French because he is still going very quickly. I am listening to the B/C/S booth, Serbian booth, which is going very fast. Can we please slow down with questions and answers. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The last four words would have been sufficient. Please proceed, and could you please slow down.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I will, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. Philipps, are you able to say whether the document in front of you appears to be a draft translation of the B/C/S document you were shown by the Defence a few minutes ago?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It looks very much like it, but I do notice that the name of the individual that signed the document is in fact missing from the draft translation, otherwise, it is a -- appears to be a draft translation of that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Might the translation please be returned to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The document that is the draft translation contains these words: "Within the scope of carrying out combat operation tasks, Marko Zubic is hereby assigned to the establishment post that exists in the corps command." Was Marko Zubic someone that you included in the chart?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will have to consult my notes for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. If it may assist you, he is described in the earlier part of the document, according to the draft translation, as a reserve major. Is someone of that rank likely to appear in the chart by name?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would depend on his position, rather than his rank. And looking at my index, I see that reserve Major Marko Zubic does appear on the chart. I can attempt to find him on a slide, if required.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And according to the document you have just consulted, was there any other reference or source as to Marko Zubic?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Apart from that document, there was a witness statement from the assistant commander for logistics.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, in due course I will seek to tender the draft translation. I ask the witness be shown another document, together with a translation. It is the only copy I have so I will ask that, firstly, the B/C/S document be placed on the ERN. Perhaps it could be placed so that we can see the ERN number which is at the top of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. Philipps, yesterday you were asked questions about the formation of the Vogosca operations tactical group. For the benefit of my learned colleagues, that question appears at page --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have the reference so that we can check. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think Mr. Ierace started a sentence to give you the reference, so it might have been wise to let him finish. And if it would have been not understandable, that you would have asked for further specifications. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. The page is 11.729, commencing at line 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You were asked whether you had any knowledge about the formation of the group and whether you knew why it was formed and whether you had any information about that. You, in essence, replied that there may be information in your list of documents. Would you please go to your list of documents and assist us as to whether the B/C/S document on the ERN -- I am sorry -- on the ELMO was one such document.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my index to the chart, I have listed under Vogosca operational tactical group ERN number Y0003262. Y0003262: an order by a Colonel Dragan Marcetic relating to the forming of the VRS TG Vogosca.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I might indicate that the document was provided by the Defence on the 12th of June, 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Would you now go to the other document and place that on the ELMO. Are you able to say whether the document now on the ELMO which is in the English language appears to be a translation of the B/C/S document for which you just gave us the ERN number.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It appears to be the same document, based on the names of the units and individuals.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And can you tell us where the document emanated from and what type of document it is, according to the information on the document.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The document has come from the corps headquarters of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps, that is, the Sarajevo Romanija Corps command, and has originated from the deputy corps commander or chief of staff, Dragan -- Colonel Dragan Marcetic, and is an order to form a Vogosca tactical or operational group from four separate brigades.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Is it dated the 19th of June, 1993?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Is it indicated in these words to be "very urgent"?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in capitals, at the top, it says: "very urgent."

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Does one of the earlier paragraphs, in essence, explain the reason for the formation of the group?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, really the first paragraph of the order is a preliminary explanation of the reason for the formation.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do the words "I order" thereafter appear in capitals?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Would you please read item one under the words "I order"?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Perhaps the camera can pan back a little.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Under the words "I order," it states: "Form the Vogosca tactical group composed of the Ilijas, Kosevo, Vogosca and Rajlovac Brigades. Lieutenant-Colonel Dragan Josipovic is commander, in addition to his regular duties."

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Would you please read part of or start to read the next paragraph?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The Vogosca TG commander will, when operations are ordered, unite the entire combat operations of these brigades in a single operational and tactical whole, with the aim of inflicting the greatest possible losses of personnel and TMS, technical equipment and materiel, on the enemy, halting enemy penetration on the specified axis, recovering lost positions in the operating zone of the units mentioned, and thereby remove the dangers to special production enterprises and create conditions for further offensive operations."

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please stop there. Do you know what the initials TMS refer to?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: TMS is a B/C/S abbreviation which refers to logistic requirements, that is, technical equipment and materiel. By that I mean ammunition and supplies required for fighting.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Might those documents be returned. Mr. President, in due course, I will seek to tender both the original and the translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Finally, Mr. Philipps, would you please go back to slide 66, about which you were asked some questions. In the box with the bold line, in particular in the middle of the box, we see a head and shoulders symbol for Mr. Ugresic. The symbol is shown with a dotted line. What does the fact that the figure that is in the dotted line indicate, if anything?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The figure itself appears dotted simply through the nature of the display. The figure should simply be blue, with a blank face, rather than dotted.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, that complete re-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ierace. Judge Nieto-Navia has one or more questions to put to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Although it is probably well-known to everybody, sometimes names change from army to army and from country to country. So I would like to know -- we don't have that in our records until now, as far as I remember. I would like to know the rank of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps, starting, let's say, from the 2nd lieutenant until General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Generally speaking, there is a laid down regulation for the rank in each position. However, within the Sarajevo Romanija Corps, the shortage of officers was such that many officers held positions that were much higher than their rank would normally afford. You would expect to see, in charge of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps, a major general. In charge of each of the brigades would be a full colonel. Each of the battalions would be commanded normally by a major in the JNA or the Sarajevo Romanija Corps. Below that, companies were commanded by captains, and below that, it is possible that platoons were commanded by 2nd lieutenants, though more normally they would be commanded by senior noncommissioned officers. Sections themselves would be commanded by ranks, a noncommissioned officer such as a lance corporal. However, in reality,, we see that in one situation a sergeant was commanding a brigade, admittedly a small brigade, but nevertheless a sergeant was in charge of quite a large organisation of a battalion size, although called a brigade. The ranks Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. did vary and so although we might see, for example, a lieutenant colonel in charge of an artillery regiment, he may later have been replaced by someone as low in rank as captain. So the variations in the ranks are quite dramatic to what you would normally expect to see in any army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Which was the rank of Genera Mladic?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would, unfortunately, be surmising on his rank at any particular point. I understood that he was a colonel general. That is one rank higher than a major general.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Thank you. No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Judge El Mahdi also has a question for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. [Interpretation] Sir, I would like to ask you to clarify point. Having done your analysis of the structure of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps, did you find out about the existence of snipers and also their relationship to the corps command, if this existed, of course.

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The term "sniper" is used very often to refer simply to someone who is shooting at a specific target. But if we are now talking about trained snipers, that is individuals who are specifically designated as snipers, then each unit of a size of a platoon, that is, a relatively small unit, should have at least one sniper attached to it. Each battalion would have a small group of snipers attached to it, and each brigade would have a sniper platoon. So, at each level, trained snipers were supposedly, that is according to the regulations, attached and under the command at that particular level. At the corps level, there is no specific sniper unit. So I have seen no specific information that there was a corps level sniping organisation. The highest level I have seen sniping unit is at a brigade level.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I have another question. Did you find out about the relationship, if any, between the corps and paramilitary formations?

utterances.speaker: RICHARD PHILIPPS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The existence of paramilitary formations, to use that term, is shown on the chart with the one example of a unit that I could not link directly to the Sarajevo Romanija Corps. And that is shown on the right-hand side of the chart. Other organisations which had been termed "paramilitary" were later shown or may have been incorporated within the corps itself, that is, were no longer paramilitary, that is outside the military, but were brought into the military and under the command of the corps. The example I have located does not appear to be part of the structure of the corps, as there is no command relationship that I have located between the corps headquarters and the paramilitary organisation, and there is no VP number or vojni post number for this organisation and it is shown on the chart under the name of the officer in charge, Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Philipps, this concludes your evidence before this Chamber. I usually thank those for coming from a long distance to this courtroom. I think that would not be appropriate. But it is not of less importance that you came and answered all the questions of the parties and of the Bench. So, therefore, thank you and -- well, the safe trip home is not as usual as well. Madam Usher, can you please escort Mr. Philipps out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, could you --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I indicated yesterday that I would seek to tender formally the additional references that were referred to. As well, this morning I indicated three other documents. I don't have copies of those documents. Would you prefer that the Prosecution made the necessary number of copies and then formally sought to tender those documents later in the day?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think that would be preferable. Because if there would be whatever objection, we might have difficulties without looking at the document, very often, to decide on objections. So, therefore, we prefer to have that done later this day. Perhaps it would then be a good idea to deal with all the documents, both Defence and Prosecution documents, at the same time subsequently and not to deal with part of them now and part of them later today.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Before I call the next witness, you may remember yesterday I pointed out that the witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I apologise but before Mr. Ierace goes on further, perhaps you could authorise us --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- for our expert to leave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... Yes, your expert out of the courtroom. Of course, it is public session, so if he wants to follow the proceedings, he is perfectly free to do so in the public gallery.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yesterday, I foreshadowed that the next witness will be marking some maps in the witness box, unless the Trial Chamber has approved for him to do it out of court. It then lapsed in the course of business of the day. So we did not ask the witness to do that yesterday afternoon. However, I have in mind, if it is acceptable to the Trial Chamber, that during one of the breaks - perhaps the first break - the witness will carry out that task so as to save court time. I raise it now in the absence of the witness so that the Trial Chamber could consider whether you think that is an appropriate course, and then the witness could be instructed, if you think it is appropriate, to do that during the break. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence would not agree with the proposal of my learned colleague that the witness should mark a map without the presence of the Defence and the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, the Chamber would prefer the marking to be done in court, but let's -- I mean, marking as such, the time it takes would be approximately the same in and out of court. So perhaps we can do it in a speedy way, of course, without making any mistakes, but that is the same in or outside court.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, perhaps -- I am sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Perhaps I should explain a little about the background of the maps, to save time. These maps comprise separate maps for each individual scheduled incident, sniping and shelling, and as well, I think the unscheduled incident number one. The maps were prepared within the OTP and indicate the confrontation lines based on information available to those who prepared the maps. The maps have been shown to the witness, and he has indicated that they are not entirely correct in terms of the position of the confrontation lines. So that is the nature of the changes that he will be making. The witnesses who prepared the maps are -- have been dropped or not included because of the pressure on the OTP to finish by the due date. I don't -- I take it view that there is nothing of significance which requires him to be called, especially since we now have the head of the relevant army who can, from his own recollection and knowledge, indicate the position of the confrontation lines. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps if you would ask the witness in general whether a map with confrontation lines on it would be correct, and if not, whether he could adjust. I mean, that would take not much time, I hope. If that --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Except that there are 30 maps, one for each incident. But perhaps, Mr. President, I can take it to a certain point in the examination-in-chief and then if you wish to reconsider, that can be done. But I will take it to a point where you will be better seized of the background and the task involved.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We will see how it develops. I take it that the 30 maps are partly overlapping each other.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I should say this: There is less than 30. Some maps refer to more than one incident.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But would the maps overlap, would the parts of a specific map overlap --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes. For instance, the Dobrinja shelling map clearly has an area which relates to some of the sniping issues. But the sniping maps necessarily in more detail because, of course, the position becomes more critical as you go down in scale.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But perhaps we would not ask a witness, if he made corrections on one map, to make the same corrections on another map where the same front lines appear.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I thought of that, Mr. President. It doesn't work.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, let's see how we can proceed. Then you are ready to call your next witness, which would be?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic. Madam Usher, would you please escort the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning. Can you hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before giving testimony in this court, Mr. Karavelic, I presume, you are required to make a solemn declaration that you will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth. The text will be handed out to you now by Madam Usher. May I invite you to make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Karavelic. Please be seated. You will first be examined by counsel for the Prosecution. Mr. Ierace, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Sir, would you please give your full name, date of birth, and rank?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC
utterances.text: My name is Vahid Karavelic. I was born on the 7th of April, 1956, in the village of Bresovik, municipality of Visoko, Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My rank --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I do not want to disturb Mr. Ierace, but sometimes it would be useful to have a visual contact with the booth. I don't know whether the Prosecution will need the chart or not. Perhaps we could avoid the problems if it is taken away. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Whenever there is any need for contact, visual contact, with the booth, and I noticed that you use visual signs several times in such a way that I am not going to accept your request. If there is anything to be communicated with the booth, it should not be done either by using your hands or other communication. If there is any problem, please address me. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Sir, I think you were about to give us your rank.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC
utterances.text: General Major.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What is your present position or occupation? Or should I say, what duties do you have?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC
utterances.text: I am currently working in the joint command of the army of the Federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina. In the joint command, I am the chief of the section for plans and operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Is that in the joint staff of the army of the Federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, in 1975, did you join the former JNA? Did you enlist?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC
utterances.text: That year, I enlisted to the first year of the military academy in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The question is very leading. It gives the year and it gives what the answer should be. I don't think it is admissible.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, you may recall that I was invited by the Defence to ask leading questions in relation to the background of witnesses called by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there any dispute as to 1975 or as to the JNA?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I don't know this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I am asking you whether that is in dispute or not. It is either "yes" or "no."

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I don't know this because the problem is the following: I cannot memorize everything and, therefore, if dates are given that I cannot memorize, the time that I find them, the procedure -- the proceedings go on. That is the reason why I am stating this.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, in the interest of saving time, I will rephrase the question. I will handle it differently.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you join the JNA? Did you enlist in the JNA?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: When?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC
utterances.text: In 1975, I went to the military academy, and in 1979 I received my first rank and I began to work in the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, ultimately, when did you leave the JNA?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC
utterances.text: I deserted from the JNA in December 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What was your rank before you deserted in December 1991? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC
utterances.text: I was a captain, first class.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Had you done further studies or attended courses from the time that you left the military academy until December 1991?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC
utterances.text: Yes. I took a large number of courses, amongst them a course for the battalion commanders in Sarajevo in 1986 which lasted for six months. This is one of the most important courses that I took. After that, I took the exam for the rank of major from 1987 to 1989, so I took this course from two years and I was awarded -- or I took the exam for the rank of major. I also attended other courses.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, following your desertion from the JNA, did you become involved in the military forces for the newly independent state of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC
utterances.text: Yes. After I left the Yugoslav People's Army, I joined the resistance -- I joined the Patriotic League of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: When did you do that, that is, when did you join the Patriotic League?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC
utterances.text: In early January 1992, I participated in the organisation and the work of the Patriotic League of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And at some stage did you become involved in the defence forces in the form of the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC
utterances.text: On the 10th of February, 1992, I was officially appointed commander of the district staff of Territorial Defence of Tuzla. And from then on, I commanded the resistance in the area from -- of north-eastern Bosnia up until the time I was captured.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. I have to intervene. There is a part missing in the French translation. "Territorial Defence" has only been interpreted as "sector," and this is important.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You mean appointed commander of the district staff of Territorial Defence of Tuzla. Yes. That has then been corrected. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In about April of 1992, did something happen to you?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC
utterances.text: On the 27th of April, 1992, I was captured and taken to Belgrade, to the -- actually, to the prison in Sremska Mitrovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Were you tried?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC
utterances.text: From April 28th until the 11th of May, I was taken before three colonels every day, three colonels of the JNA, who processed me, and at the end, they told me -- they asked me how I would like to be executed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: May I interrupt because we are under severe time constraints. I will stop you at that point and ask you a further point in a minute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So the Defence can usually cross-examine the witness later on, I see that the name of the prison or, rather, the town where the prison is located wasn't mentioned in the transcript. I know that this will be done, corrected in the night, but so that we can cross-examine today, would it be possible to ask the witness to spell the name of the town. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Might I suggest that that be done at cross-examination rather than at this stage. I am very conscious of the time constraint.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. On the other hand, I can imagine that you might need the name of that village for preparing for cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, if that is the case, then perhaps Mr. Piletta-Zanin would care to read the statement that we gave him some time ago from this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If this is in the statement, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Page two, second last sentence or third sentence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it that when a witness appears in this court and gives testimony, that the party to whom a prior statement has been disclosed uses that for the understanding of the testimony and if there would be any need to do that in cross-examination, to verify whether it is correctly understood, it can be done in cross-examination. And even if you thought it be necessary, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, it took you five lines, when one would have certainly been sufficient. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I gave Mr. Ierace now the possibility to proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, if it is possible for you to answer "yes" or "no," were you tried? In other words, was there some sort of court hearing or court-martial hearing?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC
utterances.text: I don't know what the role of those three colonels was, but I think, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And at some stage, did you receive a sentence?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC
utterances.text: After the question how I would wish to be executed, they told me that they will tell me their decision later. However, after that, there was an exchange.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: As a result of the exchange, did you retrieve your freedom?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC
utterances.text: Yes, on the 13th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: After that date, did you resume your military pursuits, your military occupation?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC
utterances.text: After a brief period of time which I took to recuperate, I joined the Main Staff of the Territorial Defence of Bosnia-Herzegovina. And then on September 1st, 1992, upon the formation of the 1st Corps of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, I was appointed deputy commander of that corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Until when were you the deputy commander of the 1st Corps?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC
utterances.text: Until the beginning of August 1993, when I was appointed the commander of that corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, did the 1st Corps play any role in the armed conflict in Sarajevo between 1992 and 1995?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC
utterances.text: The 1st Corps of the Army of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina was the main body which performed all -- the defence activities regarding Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did the 1st Corps have responsibilities of a military nature outside the armed conflict in Sarajevo? In other words, were there other arenas of military conflict under the responsibility of the 1st Corps, apart from Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: How many troops were there by, say, mid-1993 within the 1st Corps who were placed within the confrontation lines surrounding Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC
utterances.text: The 1st Corps of the Army of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, in the course of 1993, when it was -- it had the largest number of men, comprised of 74.000 to 75.000 soldiers. In the town of Sarajevo, about 45.000 soldiers were posted and the rest were on lines outside of the city of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, were women at any stage between August 1992 -- sorry -- September 1992 and August 1994, combatants within the 1st Corps?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC
utterances.text: I think that in early 1992 there were such cases, such examples. However, from the end of 1992, we stopped with this practice, for several reasons, and we kept women only in the commands in the medical corps, in logistics, and on lighter duties.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What was the earliest military age within the 1st Corps between those same dates, that is, between September 1992 and August 1994?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC
utterances.text: Eighteen. And we also did have volunteers who would be under eighteen.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In relation to the volunteers, how young were the?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC
utterances.text: They would be one or two years younger than 18, but they always had special status and we would wait for them to be 18, to reach the age of 18.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What did their special status involve? In particular, what type of duties did those volunteers between 16 and 18 carry out?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC
utterances.text: Nothing special. They were placed on waiting lists.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Well, did they have combatant duties? In other words, did the volunteers, 16 year olds and 17 year olds, perform duties as combatants on the front line, actually fighting?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC
utterances.text: No. We didn't permit that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Were the reserve police utilised by the 1st Corps as combatants at any stage in that same period of time?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What about civil defence? Were there any occasions when you would use civil defence or civil protection, as it is sometimes known, to, say, transport water or food to the troops of the 1st Corps?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC
utterances.text: If I may be allowed to stress the difference between the term "civil protection" and "military duty." The 1st Corps of the Army of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina in the course of 1993, 1994 and 1995, in short time periods, did use the men from the work obligation. Civil protection, during the entire period of the aggression, carried out its own tasks and duties.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: When you say, "men from the work obligation" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I may take it that you respond to a word used by the witness. Mr. Karavelic, this Court still has to decide on a lot of aspects of the conflict. When you use the word "aggression," we would interpret that as not aggression from your side but aggression from the Serbian side. If there is no specific need to refer to aggression and if you would, for example, you would just refer to the time of the conflict, this Chamber would prefer you to use neutral words, unless there is a specific reason why you would use another word. But the example we just had, I think you were really referring to the entire period of the armed conflict. So if you could do that. But if there is a specific reason why you choose that word in answering the questions, of course, please indicate so and we will listen to why you use that word. I think it is time for the break anyhow. Mr. Karavelic, we will adjourn. But Mr. Piletta-Zanin, if there was any issue left on from approximately 10 minutes ago you would like to submit to the Chamber, then please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There was a minute or so ago in relation to the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, it was when you asked for a clarification as far as the name of the village was concerned, where we spent some time on that and when I gave the opportunity to Mr. Ierace to proceed. I got the impression that there was perhaps some other issue that you would like to raise.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. In the meantime, the name appeared, following your intervention. It appeared in the transcript so I was able to find it, and things are clear now. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We will adjourn until 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, since the Defence has just received material which is extremely important and it is only now we received it, although we have been waiting for this for ages, we ask your Chamber for the possibility to talk about this for 10 or 15 minutes at some point so that we can get some answers from the Prosecution. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I wonder whether this issue has anything to do with the cross-examination of the present witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If not -- is it in relation to this witness, Mr. Piletta-Zanin?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Mr. President, this is not in relation with this witness. The witness may leave now and then we can talk about it, but that would mean waste of time. I just need to confer. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will then discuss the matter in due course and we know that it will not affect the testimony of this witness. So it is not urgent, we don't have to do it now, right away.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, it is urgent to discuss it today, but not right away. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We will see whether we find a moment to discuss the matter. It would assist the parties if the Chamber would have available one copy of the material so that we at least would know what we are talking about, that might save time. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Sir, before the break you told us that men who had a work obligation in short time periods were used by the 1st Corps. What do you mean by "men who had a work obligation"?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC
utterances.text: These were people, I presume, who were unfit for military service for the army. These were people who were slightly more elderly, but on the other hand, would be able to give their contribution to the work obligation which is established in the law, since the law provides for this possibility, for the state to use people in work obligation on occasions. Every now and then, the 1st Corps, the command, would ask the staff and then the staff would ask the Ministry of Defence, which would then allow or authorise the use of people in such a way of smaller units for the needs of work obligations.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What type of duties would those people do for the 1st Corps? Can you give us an example.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC
utterances.text: Building of temporary facilities, either above ground or underground for troops accommodation, for instance.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did those duties include the digging of trenches?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC
utterances.text: Perhaps, yes. Perhaps, yes, deep within the territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: When you say, "deep within the territory," do you mean not at the confrontation lines or do you mean something else?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC
utterances.text: That's precisely what I mean, not on the confrontation line.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Who would use the trenches which were dug deep within the territory? Military people? Civilians? Could you explain.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC
utterances.text: Military and civilians. For instance, most infrastructure facilities for medical facilities, for kitchens, building of roads, they would need to get supplies, then for sewage pipes and so on, for a number of different types of work.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, did the ranks, that is the upper ranks, of the 1st Corps include any Sarajevans of the Serb community?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Can you give us an example or two?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC
utterances.text: For instance, at the main staff of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the deputy commander of the main staff was General Jovo Divjak, a Serb. And then at my command, in my corps command, two of my assistants were officers of Serb nationality: My assistant for legal affairs throughout the war was Colonel Zlatko Petrovic, a Serb, and then assistant for morale in 1992 and 1993 was Colonel Rajko Mihajlovic, a Serb. And there were many others.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I want to ask you a few questions about armaments. At any stage between the dates I mentioned earlier, did the 1st Corps have tanks?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC
utterances.text: The 1st Corps, throughout the period until the summer of 1994, had only two tanks and they were inside the city. It could be also mentioned that there was a third one which was never functioning, and there was only one tank that we used for manoeuvres and used it in combat Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. and for defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What happened in the summer of 1994 in relation to your tanks, the number of tanks?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC
utterances.text: In the summer of 1994, during one battle on a wider area on a plateau between two mountains, Treskavica and Bjelasnica, the 1st Corps of the Army of BH captured a large number of tanks and APCs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if Mr. Ierace could be a little more precise in his question, in his question about the summer of 1994, if he could just be more precise, which month.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I am just going to ask for a technician, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: For what, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is the usual problem. I must have done something wrong.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is not necessary, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. Sometimes problems arise even without doing something wrong. Although the question on what part of the year 1994 could have been put to the witness in cross-examination, Mr. Ierace, I think it would be wise perhaps to follow another question to specify.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: When exactly did that happen, that your forces captured a large number of tanks and APCs? In what month?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC
utterances.text: I think that it was in September 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. I won't take that any further, for obvious reasons, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you have any rocket launchers between September 1992 and August 1994?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC
utterances.text: We had -- there was mortars and then there was rocket launchers. Could you please repeat your question? I didn't understand it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You mentioned then that there were rocket launchers. Did you have any rocket launchers that worked between September 1992 and August 1994?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC
utterances.text: A rocket launcher, there isn't such a term.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I see. Perhaps it is a translation problem. Do you understand what is meant by a multiple rocket launcher, which is a series of tubes in one unit which is capable of launching around a dozen rockets almost simultaneously so that each of the rockets lands within the same approximate target area?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC
utterances.text: We had a very small number of single rocket launchers, single tube rocket launcher. We had a multiple rocket launcher called Orkan, but throughout the period, we never had ammunition. We didn't have a single rocket for this weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you have any ammunition for the single rocket launchers in that period?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC
utterances.text: I don't think that we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In relation to the ammunition and armaments available to the Sarajevo Romanija Corps, according to your information, did they have any specialist sniping weapons in that period?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC
utterances.text: I think that the Sarajevo Romanija Corps had a high percentage of a type of sniper which their units had. I think that was the 7.9 millimetre calibre sniper 76 and it was produced by Kragujevac from Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: When you refer to 7.9, does that refer to the size of the cartridge or the size of the bullet?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC
utterances.text: I think that this is the charge size, but I think that the bullet is smaller. It is 7.62.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, might the witness be shown a map from the exhibit list. Excuse me. That is 3644.VK-3. Mr. President, it may be that the Madam Registrar does not have a copy. I have a bundle here, so I will hand those over to the court usher. I think the Defence has a copy, Mr. President. It was included on our exhibit list.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence has VK-2, and Mr. Ierace said VK-3, so we want to make sure that there is no confusion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are you using V-2 or --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: VK-3. I think it is the same map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, then it is at least confusing to give it different numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: It won't all fit on the ELMO, so perhaps that first can simply be handed to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, is VK-2 going to be used for other purposes? I mean, it's --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I suspect that in fact is an error, and there is only one map, and for some reason it has been given two separate numbers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see from a distance that Ms. Pilipovic had a similar size map in her hand, but it is not the same one.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. This VK-2 has no markings. It is the same scale but this VK-2 doesn't have markings and VK-3 has some markings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You have got VK-3 now, Mr. Piletta-Zanin? Okay, then please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, it wasn't an error. They are separate maps.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Sir, do you recognise the map which is in front of you?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, just so that we agree on the numbers, this is VK-3 or VK-2 that we need?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: VK-3.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Three.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you recognise that map?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Would you please read out the words which appear in heavy black marker pen across the top of the map.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC
utterances.text: "Command posts of the command of the 1st Corps and of the brigades of the 1st Corps of the Army of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina in 1993."

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In the bottom right-hand corner, does your name appear, together with your signature, indicated as the Commandant, that is, Commander?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: On the map we can see marked, with a blue pen, a number of sites and symbols. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Some of those symbols and positions appear in the city and some to the north of the city. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I will first ask you about the blue pen markings in the city. And perhaps at this stage the part of the map which shows some symbols in the left hand part of the city could be placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the second microphone of the witness please be switched on. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Usher, would you please switch on the other microphone of the witness as well. Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: To assist the court usher, they are numbered and perhaps we could put on the screen the portion which shows numbers one, two, and three. That is approximately in the centre of the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic, so as to assist us, would you please take the pointer that the usher will shortly hand you -- yes, and can you hold the pointer on position number one so that the camera can be adjusted. Not on the screen, but on the map itself.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You will need some adjustment to the map. Sir, we will now move the map so that we can all see where you are pointing.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC
utterances.text: The position number one, this is the location where the command of the 1st Corps of the BH army was.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: For the benefit of the transcript, there are a number of symbols that have a number one. I think there are two, to be precise. The position that the witness now points to is directly south of the stadium. Now, you said that was the location of the command of the 1st Corps of the BH army. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What was at that site? In other words, what type of building was it?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC
utterances.text: It was a building until 1992. It was the seat of a political party.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did the building have a name?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC
utterances.text: I don't believe that it had a special name, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: How many floors did the building have?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC
utterances.text: It had two floors.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did the command occupy the entire building or only part of the building?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC
utterances.text: The whole building.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Was the building ever hit between September 1992 and August 1994 by fire which you understood to come from forces of the SRK?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Several times, once directly from a tank projectile.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: When you say, "by a tank projectile," do you know whether that was in the mode of direct fire? In other words, was it possible from the building to see SRK-held territory?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC
utterances.text: Yes, 360 degrees. At the smallest possible angle, there was a gap that was found between the buildings, and a tank projectile arrived from the Grdonj region and hit the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Approximately when was that?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC
utterances.text: I think it was in the summer of 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Was there ever a policy that, or an agreement, that you and the SRK command --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am objecting to this because I think this will be a leading question. It is the way that the question is phrased that this seems to me to be the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I can inform the Trial Chamber that in the culture of common law, criminal matters, it is not only permissible but indeed is a requirement that witnesses have put to them propositions which may not be of assistance -- well, if I would put it is a different way, propositions which the witness is ideally placed to respond to and which require a confrontation, in other words, require a response from that obvious witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, of course. But a line has to be drawn between -- I mean, the most perfect way of assisting a witness is, of course, to put part of the answer in the question. I am not saying that you did, but it is not -- could you perhaps first enquire of the witness whether any specific arrangements were ever made in respect of headquarters, which I think is the basis of your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: As you please, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: General, were there any specific arrangements, as you understood it, made between the warring parties in respect of targeting or not targeting headquarters?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Would you please now move to the box marked "1," which I think is just to the right of box marked "1." Not immediately to the right but a little further to the right. Now, I think the box marked 1 had nothing inside it, whereas the box marked 2 has a cross inside it, that is, from opposite angles of the rectangle. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What does that symbol indicate?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC
utterances.text: It indicates the location of the brigade command.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I appreciate that, but the symbol of a rectangle with a cross, does that have any particular meaning?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC
utterances.text: I am not sure myself. I think perhaps it is just -- indicates the level of the establishment unit or the formation.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, you can take the pointer away for a moment. On the map we see a number of similar boxes, that is, rectangles with crosses. Do each of those indicate brigade command headquarters?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC
utterances.text: Yes. These do indicate precisely that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I will now ask you to point to a box which has a slightly different symbol. Would you please move to the left of the city, and do you see there a number of other boxes marked consecutively from 1 which have not only a cross, but also a vertical line? If you could move further to the left rather than to the right. In other words, to the west of the -- yes, stop there. I see that you are pointing to such a box, in fact, to the right.
